text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Prominent Nigerian lawyer Rotimi Williams appeals against a court ruling that he cannot represent detained presidential claimant Moshood Abiola in his treason trial.
- Nigeria's Central Bank refunds 2.6 billion naira stabilisation securities to commercial banks as part of its effort to regulate the economy.
- Nigeria's military government plans to buy off more than 400,000 bales of excess cotton from farmers.
- Democracy is the only way to improve strained ties between Nigeria and the United States, Walter Carrington, American ambassador to Nigeria says.
- Nigeria sets up Customs Processing Unit to help improve clearance of imported goods.
- Nigerians spend almost 10 billion naira annually on buying and maintaining power generators, a necessity because of poor public electricity supply, power minister says.
- Authorities start compiling names of companies and individuals to face tribunal on failed government contracts, official sources say.

- Nigerian mobile phone company Intercellular, one of nine private firms granted licences to provide full network services, signs a 540 million naira contract with American phone firm Motorolla to provide 10,000 subscriber lines next year.
